entry.title: Recycle Bin File Preview 1.0.0
entry.content:
Recycle Bin File Preview

Use the built-in Windows File Explorer Preview Pane (Alt + P) to view files in the Recycle Bin without restoring them.

The image compares the default Recycle Bin view with the preview enabled by this mod.

How to use

  1. Open the Recycle Bin in File Explorer.
  2. Press Alt + P to show the Preview Pane.
  3. Select a file to see its preview.

The mod uses your Windows file associations and installed preview handlers. It does not add new preview handlers or codecs.

Limitations

  • File types without preview support in normal Explorer folders may still show No preview available in the Recycle Bin.
  • The mod does not let you browse inside deleted folders.
  • It does not restore, copy, edit or delete your files.
  • Windows updates can change how the Recycle Bin works.

Troubleshooting

Enable Debug logging in the mod settings and look for messages starting with RBP: in the Windhawk log. Keep logging off during normal use.

Project

Source code and issue reports

Author: Luiz Bizzio. Licensed under MIT.

entry.title: Quick Settings Media Progress Bar 1.2.12
entry.content:
Quick Settings Media Progress Bar for Windows 11

Adds a modern, interactive seek bar and live playback timestamps directly to the default Windows 11 Quick Settings (Win + A) media player widget.

Features

  • Interactive Seeking & Scrubbing: Click or drag the progress bar thumb to seek smoothly within any playing track.
  • Mouse Wheel Scrubbing: Hover anywhere over the progress bar and scroll the mouse wheel to seek forward or backward.
  • Accurate Timestamps: Displays current playback time and total track duration (or remaining time).
  • Smooth Playback Sync: Automatically syncs with Windows System Media Transport Controls (SMTC) in real time across Spotify, Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, Apple Music, VLC, Windows Media Player, and more.
  • Accidental Click Protection: Interacting with the progress bar or timestamps will not trigger the underlying card button that opens the media application.
  • Native Fluent Styling: Seamlessly matches Windows 11 Fluent design, with optional system accent color tracking and zero clipping of the media card.
  • Multi-Session Support: Seamlessly switches timeline and position when switching between active media apps using the Quick Settings arrows.
  • Zero XAML Diagnostics Conflicts: Uses direct COM-interface symbol hooks in ControlCenter.dll, completely avoiding XAML Diagnostics. Fully compatible with Windows 11 Taskbar Styler, Notification Center Styler, and File Explorer Styler.
  • Auto-Restoring: Cleanly restores the native media player card when the mod is disabled or unloaded.

Credits

  • ControlCenter discovery logic adapted with appreciation from Refined Quick Settings and Sound by HeyOkay.

entry.title: Recycle Bin Tray 1.0.0
entry.content:
Recycle Bin Tray

A lightweight Windhawk Windows 11 mod that places an interactive Recycle Bin directly into your system tray.

The icon follows the current Recycle Bin state, can optionally disappear when the bin is empty, reacts to Windows Shell notifications, and supports multiple rendering styles, themes, and configurable mouse actions.

The mod is designed to remain lightweight and self-contained while integrating with the native Windows Shell wherever possible.

Features

⚠️ Drag & Drop is disabled by default. Enable Enable drag & drop in the mod settings to use this feature.

  • Drag & Drop to Recycle Bin — drag files and folders directly from the Desktop, File Explorer, or other applications that expose dropped files through the standard Windows CF_HDROP format. Deletion follows the Windows Recycle Bin policy for each source drive. If the icon is in the ^ notification-area overflow menu, open the menu and drop directly onto the Recycle Bin icon.
  • Live Recycle Bin state — updates when items are added to or removed from the Recycle Bin.
  • Four icon styles:
  • system — use the native Windows Recycle Bin icon.
  • vector — render a lightweight custom vector Windows 11-style icon.
  • font — render a glyph from an installed font family.
  • custom — load an .ico, .png, .bmp, or .jpg file.
  • Three vector variants — choose between a minimal geometric style with a lifted-lid full state, a Fluent-inspired trapezoidal style, and a compact symbolic style.
  • Separate icons for states and themes — custom mode uses Empty/Full Light-theme files with optional Empty/Full Dark-theme alternatives.
  • Optional auto-hide — automatically hides the tray icon while the Recycle Bin is empty.
  • Light / dark theme support — vector and font rendering adapt to the current Windows system theme; custom icons use Light-theme source files, optional Dark-theme alternatives, and can automatically adapt transparent monochrome image colors to the active theme.
  • Automatic recovery — a configurable fallback timer periodically checks the Recycle Bin state in case a Shell notification is missed.
  • Taskbar restart recovery — the tray icon is recreated after Explorer or the Windows taskbar is restarted.
  • DPI-aware rendering — the render target follows the tray's DPI, while Shell-reported tray geometry is tracked separately for layout changes. Vector icons are rendered at high internal resolution for smoother results.
  • Configurable mouse actions — independently configure left click, double-click, middle click, and right click.
  • Recycle Bin context menu — open, empty, or open Properties using Windows Shell-provided localized labels when available.
  • Optional empty confirmation — keep or disable the confirmation dialog before emptying the Recycle Bin.

Installation

From Windhawk

  1. Open Windhawk.
  2. Go to the Explore tab and search for Recycle Bin Tray.
  3. Click Details, then click Install.
  4. Open the mod's settings to customize the icon and mouse actions.

Manual Installation from Source

  1. Install and open Windhawk.
  2. Click Create Mod.
  3. Copy the mod source code and paste it over the template code.
  4. Click Compile Mod and enable the mod.

The mod runs as a dedicated Windhawk tool mod rather than being injected into explorer.exe, isolating it from the Windows Shell (see Mods as tools).

No separate installation, executable, or Windows service is required. Windhawk manages the process automatically.

Using the Tray Icon

The tray icon provides configurable actions for each supported mouse input.

Mouse actions

| Input | Available actions | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | | Left click | Open, context menu, empty, Properties, do nothing | | Double-click | Open, empty, Properties, do nothing | | Middle click | Empty, open, context menu, Properties, do nothing | | Right click | Context menu, open, empty, Properties, do nothing |

Each action can be configured independently from the Windhawk settings.

Click / double-click behavior

Windows sends a single-click notification before it can determine whether a second click will arrive.

When a double-click action is enabled, the mod therefore waits for the Windows double-click interval before executing the single-click action.

This small delay is intentional. Removing it while keeping independent single- and double-click actions could cause a physical double-click to execute the configured single-click action as well.

Single-click execution is deferred by the Windows double-click interval so that a physical double-click executes only its configured double-click action. If Double click action = Do nothing, a physical double-click therefore performs no action.

Drag & Drop

Drag & Drop is disabled by default. Enable Enable drag & drop in the mod settings before using this feature. When enabled, the feature uses a global low-level mouse hook (WH_MOUSE_LL) to detect the start of drag gestures.

The Recycle Bin tray icon can then be used as a normal drag & drop destination for files and folders.

Simply drag one or more items from:

  • the Windows Desktop;
  • File Explorer;
  • other applications that expose file lists through the standard Windows CF_HDROP format;

and drop them directly onto the Recycle Bin tray icon.

The mod receives the dropped items through the standard Windows OLE drag & drop mechanism and asks the Windows Shell to process them according to the Recycle Bin policy configured for each source drive.

Deletion policy and safety

Drag & drop follows the per-drive Recycle Bin policy configured in Windows for each dropped item.

If a drive is configured to remove files immediately instead of moving them to the Recycle Bin, items dropped from that drive can be permanently deleted. The Windows delete-confirmation preference is respected.

If Windows cannot recycle a selection, for example because it exceeds the configured Recycle Bin capacity, the Shell may display its native warning or confirmation before allowing permanent deletion. Cancelling that prompt leaves the operation uncompleted.

Visibility and overflow menu

For drag & drop to remain available, Hide when empty must be turned off so the Recycle Bin icon continues to exist as a target.

Windows may place the icon in the ^ notification-area overflow menu when it first appears.

Keeping it visible is recommended for quicker access.

The icon does not need to stay permanently visible in the main system tray.

  • If it is visible directly in the tray, drop files and folders onto it normally.
  • If it is in the ^ overflow menu, open the menu and drop files and folders directly onto the Recycle Bin icon.

If you want to keep the icon permanently visible, move it out of the overflow menu:

  • Manual placement: Drag the icon out of the overflow menu and place it directly in the main system tray area. Windows will remember this placement.
  • Windows Settings (if available): Go to Settings → Personalization → Taskbar → Other system tray icons and toggle the icon to On.
  • Windhawk alternative: On modern Windows 11 builds where native toggles may be missing or restricted, you can use the Always show all taskbar tray icons mod to keep all icons permanently visible.

Desktop focus behavior

Windows Explorer may occasionally fail to initiate a drag from a Desktop file when another application currently has focus.

For example, clicking a Desktop file and immediately moving the mouse may be interpreted primarily as a focus or selection operation instead of starting the drag.

This happens before the drag operation reaches the mod and is related to normal Explorer Desktop behavior.

Workarounds

Two simple workarounds are available:

Option 1 — focus the Desktop first

Click the file once without dragging, then start the drag operation again.

Option 2 — hold the mouse button briefly

Press and hold the left mouse button for approximately 500 ms before moving the file.

Once Explorer has successfully initiated the drag operation, dropping the item onto the Recycle Bin works normally.

The mod does not synthesize or force a Desktop drag when Explorer has not started an OLE drag operation. A low-level mouse hook is used only to arm the tray drop overlay; the actual data transfer still requires the source application to start normal OLE drag & drop.

Context Menu

The optional Recycle Bin context menu contains:

  • Open
  • Empty Recycle Bin — disabled when the bin is already empty
  • Properties

Menu labels are loaded from localized shell32.dll resources when available, so they follow the current Windows display language. The popup itself uses native Win32 menu rendering without custom menu icons.

English fallback strings are used when a corresponding Shell resource cannot be loaded.

Emptying the Recycle Bin

The Confirm before emptying option controls confirmation for actions that empty the Recycle Bin through the mod, independently of the Windows Display delete confirmation dialog option in Recycle Bin Properties.

When enabled, the standard Windows confirmation dialog is shown before the Recycle Bin is emptied.

When disabled, the mod requests the silent empty operation directly.

For emptying actions triggered through the mod, this setting takes precedence over the Windows Recycle Bin confirmation preference.

Icon Styles

Choose one icon style: System · Vector · Font · Custom Icon

System

Uses the Windows Shell's own Recycle Bin icon.

This is the simplest option and generally provides the closest match to the native Windows appearance.

Vector

The icon is generated at runtime with GDI+ instead of loading an image file.

It is designed for a clean Windows 11-style appearance and is rendered at a 4× internal resolution before being reduced to the final tray size for smoother edges.

Three variants are available:

  • Style 1 — minimal geometric 24×24 silhouette. The empty state uses a closed lid; the full state lifts the lid and exposes two compact content shapes while keeping the body unchanged.
  • Style 2 — Fluent-inspired trapezoidal body optimized for tray-size rendering. The empty state uses a clean outline, while the full state uses the same silhouette with a filled body.
  • Style 3 — compact symbolic silhouette with a simple lid, handle, and body. The empty state uses an outlined body, while the full state uses the same silhouette with a filled body.

Font

The icon is drawn from glyphs provided by installed font families.

The empty and full states have separate font family / typeface, glyph, and font weight settings. Font and glyph fields are intentionally blank by default: if Font mode is selected without a usable configuration, the mod falls back to the native Windows Recycle Bin icon.

Font names are matched against GDI font/typeface names exposed by Windows. Leading/trailing whitespace and surrounding quotation marks are ignored when settings are loaded. GDI limits the requested typeface name to 31 characters (LF_FACESIZE - 1); longer names are rejected instead of being silently truncated.

The Font weight option is available independently for the Empty and Full states and supports the standard Windows range from Thin (100) to Black (900). Use the base family/typeface name with the desired weight when Windows exposes the family through normal weight matching. If Windows exposes a variant as a separate typeface (for example Font Awesome 7 Free Solid or Arial Narrow), enter that exact Windows typeface name instead. When an exact weight is unavailable, Windows can select the nearest available weight in the requested family.

Fallback behavior

Font mode validates both the requested font family and glyph before rendering:

  • Empty state: if the empty-state font or glyph is unavailable, the full-bin font/glyph configuration is used automatically.
  • Full state: if the full-bin font or glyph is unavailable, the native Windows Recycle Bin icon is used.
  • If the empty state falls back to the full configuration and that configuration is also unavailable, the native Windows Recycle Bin icon is used.

This lets a font with only one suitable trash/delete glyph remain usable without showing a missing-glyph square.

Entering a glyph code

Glyph values can be entered as hexadecimal Unicode code points with or without the 0x prefix.

Examples:

0xF014
F014

To find a code point, you can use:

  • Windows Character Map (charmap.exe) to inspect installed fonts.
  • The documentation/reference of the font you are using.
  • Microsoft's references for Segoe Fluent Icons or Segoe MDL2 Assets when using those font families.

Recommended fonts & glyphs

| Font Family | State / role | Glyph Code | Notes | | --------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------- | ----- | | Font Awesome 7 Free | Empty | 0xF014 | Recommended example for the empty state. | | Font Awesome 7 Free Solid | Full | 0xF014 | Recommended example for the full state. | | Segoe Fluent Icons (Built-in, default Windows 11 icon font) | Single state | 0xE74D | Delete; no distinct empty/full Recycle Bin pair. Best used with Hide when empty enabled. | | Segoe MDL2 Assets (Built-in, legacy Windows icon font) | Single state | 0xE74D | Delete; no distinct empty/full Recycle Bin pair. Best used with Hide when empty enabled. | | Material-Design-Iconic-Font | Full | 0xF154 | Optional third-party example. |

The two built-in Segoe icon fonts are useful when a single Delete symbol is sufficient. Because they don't provide distinct empty and full Recycle Bin states, they work best with Hide when empty enabled and the Delete glyph configured for the full state: the tray icon is then hidden while the Recycle Bin is empty and shown when it contains items. If you want an always-visible icon with visually distinct empty and full states, another font is preferable.

Custom Icon

Custom mode accepts:

  • .ico
  • .png
  • .bmp
  • .jpg

Images are automatically resized to match the current system tray icon target size.

For the cleanest raster result, use artwork designed to remain readable at small tray sizes. Ideally, use a source close to the active tray target size or a clean integer multiple of it (for example 16×16, 32×32, 48×48, or 64×64 when appropriate). Avoid oversized raster artwork with hairline details: a stroke that looks clean in the source can become sub-pixel when Windows renders the tray at 16 px (100% scaling), where no resampling method can fully reconstruct the original visual weight. The actual tray target depends on the Windows display scale factor; refer to the Theme and DPI Handling table below.

Custom Icon color handling can either preserve the colors stored in the selected source image or Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to the active theme. Theme adaptation reads the selected image's alpha channel, downsamples it by exact pixel-area coverage, and recolors the resulting mask in memory for the active Light or Dark theme. At the smallest 16 px Dark-theme target, a small stroke-preservation and coverage adjustment helps thin monochrome artwork retain more visual weight. For best results, still use simple transparent monochrome artwork designed to remain readable at small sizes; very fine raster details can remain softer at 100% display scaling. No source file is modified. Native .ico files and images without an alpha channel keep their original colors.

For transparent monochrome images, the Light theme Empty and Full files are normally enough. If a Dark-theme field is blank, the corresponding Light-theme file is reused automatically. The optional Dark theme section is only needed when you want different source artwork in Dark theme.

| If you want… | Use | | --- | --- | | Keep the icon's original colors | Keep original image colors | | Automatically match a transparent monochrome icon to the Light/Dark theme | Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to theme | | Use different artwork in Dark theme | Configure the optional Dark theme image |

Looking for ready-made icons? Icons8 is a useful resource for finding icons suitable for custom .ico / .png files.

For .ico files, a multi-size icon containing a 16×16 px layer is recommended for a crisp tray result.

You can paste a Windows path copied with Copy as path directly into the setting, including the quotation marks added by Windows. The mod automatically removes surrounding quotes and unnecessary whitespace.

Examples:

[Light theme → Empty bin] "C:\Users\YourUsername\Pictures\recycle_empty.png"
[Light theme → Full bin]  D:\CustomIcons\recycle_full.png
[Dark theme → Full bin]   D:\CustomIcons\recycle_full_dark.ico

Local paths are strongly recommended for optimal performance and to avoid delays if a network share is unavailable or goes to sleep.

Custom mode uses two Light-theme source files plus optional Dark-theme alternatives:

| Recycle Bin state | Light-theme file | Optional Dark-theme file | | ----------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------ | | Empty | customIcon.light.empty | customIcon.dark.empty | | Full | customIcon.light.full | customIcon.dark.full |

The Light-theme file is always selected in Light theme. In Dark theme, the matching Dark-theme file is selected when configured; otherwise the Light-theme file is reused automatically. When Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to the active theme is selected, the selected transparent monochrome image is recolored in memory for the current theme.

When a custom file cannot be loaded, the mod automatically falls back to the Windows system Recycle Bin icon.

Recycle Bin State Detection

The mod uses Windows Shell APIs to query the current Recycle Bin state and register for Shell notifications.

The current state and tray icon are initialized immediately. The first Shell notification subscription is established after a short Explorer/taskbar stabilization window and uses Windows' SHCNRF_NewDelivery delivery mode.

Shell notifications allow the icon to react quickly when items are added to or removed from the Recycle Bin. A configurable fallback timer periodically checks the actual state in case a notification is missed.

The default fallback interval is 300 seconds and can be changed in the Windhawk settings. DPI and tray-geometry changes are handled through Windows display/DPI events and the Shell-reported tray rectangle. Bounded startup retries handle cases where the Shell or tray is not yet ready.

Theme and DPI Handling

The tray icon is regenerated when Windows reports a relevant theme or display configuration change.

The mod derives its icon render target from the tray/display DPI.

| Scale Factor | Icon Size | | ------------ | --------- | | 100% | 16×16 px | | 125% | 20×20 px | | 150% | 24×24 px | | 200% | 32×32 px | | 250% | 40×40 px | | 300% | 48×48 px | | 400% | 64×64 px |

The target size is obtained from the current tray/display DPI. The rectangle returned by Shell_NotifyIconGetRect is tracked separately as a geometry-change signal; its slot bounds are not treated as a documented HICON target size.

Vector icons are rendered internally at 4× the target resolution before being downsampled with high-quality interpolation to fit the active tray size. This reduces jagged edges while keeping rendering and memory usage low.

Taskbar / Explorer Restart Recovery

The mod listens for the standard TaskbarCreated message.

When Windows Explorer or the taskbar is restarted, the mod recreates the tray icon automatically.

This allows the icon to recover without requiring the Windhawk mod to be manually restarted.

Technical Notes

  • The tray icon is hosted by a hidden top-level tool window owned by the mod's dedicated tray thread.
  • Drag & drop uses the standard Windows OLE IDropTarget mechanism and accepts dropped file lists exposed through CF_HDROP.
  • Dropped items are processed asynchronously on a dedicated STA worker through IFileOperation, so Shell UI or slow storage does not block the source application's DoDragDrop call. The worker is created lazily on the first accepted drop.
  • A passive IFileOperationProgressSink tracks operation results and logs failures without changing the Shell operation.
  • The mod does not create a separate executable or Windows service.
  • GDI+ is initialized lazily only when vector rendering or custom raster-image loading requires it; native .ico loading can bypass GDI+. Once initialized, it stays available for the lifetime of the tool and is released during final teardown.
  • Tray timers are explicitly cancelled during window destruction before icon and Shell resources are released.
  • Explorer/taskbar restarts are detected through the standard TaskbarCreated broadcast received by the hidden tray host.
  • The current icon handle is explicitly destroyed whenever the icon is replaced or the mod unloads.
  • The tray thread uses Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness, follows the rectangle reported by Shell_NotifyIconGetRect, and tracks slot geometry changes independently from the DPI-derived render size.
  • A transparent top-level helper window provides the physical per-monitor DPI reference and is also used as the OLE drop overlay when drag & drop is enabled.
  • Explorer owns notification-area placement. If Windows exposes the tray on multiple taskbars, drag & drop follows the single icon rectangle returned by the Shell API.
  • A low-level mouse hook runs on a dedicated message-pump thread only while drag & drop support is enabled to detect the beginning and end of a potential drag; OLE IDropTarget remains responsible for the actual drop.

Settings Reference

The Windhawk settings are grouped by function:

  • General — visibility and icon style.
  • Vector — vector variant selection.
  • Font — font family and glyph values for empty/full states.
  • Custom Icon — color handling, Light-theme Empty/Full source files, and optional Dark-theme files.
  • Actions — mouse-button behavior and empty confirmation.
  • System — fallback Recycle Bin state refresh interval.

Renderer-specific settings only apply to the corresponding selected icon style.

For example, the Vector section is used only when Icon style is set to Vector.

Troubleshooting

The icon does not appear

Check that the Recycle Bin is not empty if auto-hide is enabled.

If the icon is still missing:

  1. Disable and re-enable the mod in Windhawk.
  2. Try restarting Windhawk.
  3. Check whether Windows has moved the icon into the notification-area overflow menu (^).

Windows may place the icon in the overflow menu when it first appears. This is normal. If you want it permanently visible, drag it from the overflow menu into the main system tray area; Windows will remember the placement.

Drag & Drop does not work

  1. Check the mod's settings to ensure that Drag & Drop is enabled and Hide when empty is turned off.
  2. If the icon is in the ^ overflow menu, open the overflow panel and drop onto the Recycle Bin icon itself.
  3. Make sure the source application provides dropped files through the standard Windows CF_HDROP format.

If dragging from the Desktop does not work, check whether another application currently has the input focus.

In that situation, either:

  • click the Desktop/file once before starting the drag; or
  • hold the left mouse button for approximately 500 ms before moving the file.

The dark theme does not apply

Check your Windows personalization settings to ensure that global dark mode is active.

For custom icons:

  • with Original colors, add an optional Dark-theme file if you want different artwork or colors in Dark theme;
  • with Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to the active theme, use a transparent monochrome image with an alpha channel. Native .ico files and images without an alpha channel keep their original colors.

Custom icons do not display

Verify that:

  • the configured path is correct;
  • the file exists and is accessible;
  • the image format is supported;
  • the selected Color handling mode matches the type of image you are using.

For raster images, choose a source size appropriate for the current display scale using the Theme and DPI Handling table; thin diagonal strokes can retain some aliasing at very small tray sizes. For .ico files, a multi-size icon containing a 16×16 px image is recommended.

If a custom icon cannot be loaded, the mod automatically falls back to the Windows system Recycle Bin icon.

A font glyph does not display

Check that:

  • the configured Font name exactly matches the Windows GDI font/typeface name;
  • the Glyph value is a valid Unicode hexadecimal code point (for example 0xF014);
  • the selected font actually contains a glyph at that hexadecimal code point.

If either the font name or glyph code is incorrect or unavailable, Font mode falls back according to the rules described in the Font section above.

entry.title: WinKlok 1.0.0
entry.content:
WinKlok

A calmer, smarter clock mod for Windows 11 taskbar. WinKlok replaces the stock date/time flyout with a fast, native, Fluent-styled panel that combines a Calendar, Stopwatch, Timer, Alarm, Notes and Settings in one place, and puts live stopwatch and timer previews right next to the taskbar clock.

Highlights

| | | |---|---| | Native look and feel | Drawn with Direct2D and DirectWrite in the Windows palette, with real acrylic blur, your accent colour, light and dark themes, and Windows-style slide-up animations. | | Everything in one panel | Calendar, Stopwatch, Timer, Alarm, Notes and Settings, one click away from the clock. | | Live taskbar previews | A running stopwatch or timer is shown beside the clock with pause/play and reset buttons. | | Smooth scrolling | Mouse wheel, precision touchpad (tracked from raw two-finger movement with kinetic momentum), touch and pen share smooth scrolling. | | Private by design | No network access, no telemetry, no accounts. Everything is stored locally by Windhawk. |

Features

Calendar

  • Month, year and decade views, with smooth vertical month scrolling like the Windows calendar.
  • Today and the selected date are marked with your accent colour. First day of the week follows Windows.

Stopwatch

  • Centisecond precision, up to 200 laps (the newest lap is always on top) and a smooth lap list.
  • Keeps running while the panel is closed and shows a live preview next to the clock.

Timer

  • Hours / minutes / seconds pickers, optional timer names and one-click presets you can save and remove.
  • Run several timers at once. The most recently touched timer is shown beside the clock.

Alarm

  • Repeat on any days, custom label, snooze length and one of nine built-in sounds with live audition.
  • The sound and snooze length you pick become the defaults for your next alarm.
  • If an alarm or timer came due while the PC was off or asleep, it never rings late. One popup lists everything you missed, with dates and times.

Notes

  • Any number of notes, saved automatically, with a rich preview of Markdown and LaTeX maths.
  • Paste from ChatGPT, Gemini, Google and the web and keep the structure: headings, lists, tables, block quotes, code blocks, links and equations are converted to Markdown as you paste.
  • Links in the preview are clickable (only the link itself), plain URLs are detected automatically.
  • One-tap Copy button for the whole note body (the title is not included), adjustable text size.

Settings

  • Taskbar previews, preview layout, notification icon, 12/24-hour time (applied everywhere), panel material (acrylic or simple) and default timer / alarm sounds.
  • Sync time now (Windows asks for administrator permission whenever it is needed).
  • A compact About card with the version, developer and project links.

First-run defaults

Notification bell off, taskbar previews on, time format following Windows, acrylic blur, side-by-side layout, the Windows Alarm tone for both timers and alarms.

Getting started

  1. Install and enable the mod in Windhawk.
  2. WinKlok takes over the taskbar clock within a second or so. If the clock does not change, restart Windows Explorer from Task Manager.
  3. Have fun…

Tips

  • Scroll over the tab bar to reveal more tabs, or click a tab to slide it to the centre.
  • Right-click a timer preset to reveal its remove button.
  • The notification bell is optional. Turn it off in Settings if you prefer the stock one.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11 with the XAML taskbar, 64-bit only.
  • Do not combine with other mods that rebuild the taskbar clock area (for example Taskbar Clock Customization) until you have verified they coexist.
  • WinKlok does not change the taskbar height. Use the Taskbar height and icon size mod for that.
  • To turn WinKlok off, disable the mod in Windhawk: the taskbar clock goes back to Windows immediately.
  • If something misbehaves, enable logging for this mod in Windhawk and check the log.

For developers

  • Single-file C++ mod, organised in blocks: engine and persistence, taskbar integration (XAML injection and hooks), native UI primitives, sound synthesis, rich-text and LaTeX engine, panel pages and alert windows.
  • Rendering is plain Win32 + Direct2D/DirectWrite. There is no browser engine and no external asset.
  • Alarm sounds are synthesised at runtime into in-memory WAV buffers, so nothing needs to be shipped.
  • The pasted-HTML to Markdown converter lives next to the Notes editor and understands the clipboard HTML Format produced by modern browsers and chat apps.
  • Contributions, bug reports and ideas are welcome on GitHub.

Credits and licence

Made by Shifting Whistler.

  • GitHub: https://github.com/shifting-whistler
  • WinKlok Repo: https://github.com/shifting-whistler/WinKlok

WinKlok is free and open source software released under the GNU General Public License v3.0 (or any later version). You are free to use, study, share and improve it under the terms of that licence.

entry.title: Fast Backspace 1.0
entry.content:
Fast Backspace

Increase the speed of held Backspace without changing the repeat speed of other keys. The first press and the Windows keyboard repeat delay stay unchanged.

Settings

Set Backspace speed multiplier to an integer from 1 to 10. The default is 2; 1 keeps normal Windows speed. Changes take effect immediately. Values outside this range are clamped. Start with a low value to avoid deleting too much.

Behavior

  • Single presses stay normal. Acceleration starts when Windows repeats a held physical Backspace key.
  • Ctrl, Alt, Shift, and Windows-key combinations are not accelerated. Pressing another key during a hold cancels acceleration until Backspace is released.
  • A repeat observed in a different foreground window cancels acceleration for that hold.
  • Repeats arrive in small batches, which can feel bursty at high multipliers. Actual deletion speed depends on the application.

How it works

A dedicated Windhawk tool process uses a global keyboard hook to observe repeats and queues bounded extra key-downs through SendInput outside the callback. Extra events retain the source scan code; the physical key-up releases Backspace, and stale input is discarded after release, cancellation, or shutdown.

Compatibility and limitations

Designed for Windows 10 and 11 and applications that accept synthetic keyboard input. The mod runs independently of Explorer and does not inject into each app.

  • Elevated apps, games, raw-input apps, remappers, accessibility tools, and remote sessions may reject or handle injected input differently. The mod does not bypass Windows integrity restrictions or operate on the secure desktop.
  • Backspace is accelerated wherever it is handled, including password fields and non-text actions such as navigation. The global hook cannot reliably identify text fields. Disable the mod where this behavior is undesirable.
  • Foreground-window checks cannot detect every change of focus inside one window or an application-specific mode change. Release Backspace before changing focus.
  • Other hooks can block injected input. Windows can also silently remove a low-level hook if its thread times out; disable and re-enable the mod to retry.
  • Disabling the mod cancels pending work and removes its hook. Input already delivered to an application cannot be undone. Physical input is passed through.

Troubleshooting

If Backspace is not faster, check that the multiplier exceeds 1, release and hold the key again without modifiers, and try an ordinary, non-elevated text editor. Disable and re-enable the mod if necessary. Windhawk logs initialization and input-insertion failures when logging is enabled. Failed batches are not retried.

entry.title: RetroBar Clock Flyout Fix 1.0.0
entry.content:
RetroBar Clock Flyout Fix

This mod fixes the borders of the clock flyout to restore the Aero borders. It is made specifically for RetroBar's Aero (Windows Vista/7 style) clock/calendar flyout. This modification has been tested on Windows 10 21H2.

Screenshots

Before

After

When Clock click action is set to the Aero calendar, RetroBar creates the flyout inside its own process (it instantiates the COM class from timedate.cpl and calls ShowFlyout), then nudges the window next to the taskbar. This mod therefore runs in RetroBar.exe and:

  • It gives the flyout the thick Aero frame and keeps it non-resizable;
  • It keeps it floating away from the work area edges, also after RetroBar repositions it.

On Windows 10 the Win32 clock flyout must be available (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ImmersiveShell\UseWin32TrayClockExperience = 1).

Credits & Reference

  • RetroBar by dremin — the taskbar that hosts the Aero clock flyout.
  • Aero Flyout Fix by aubymori — timedate.cpl hooks and flyout positioning logic.
  • xoascf - Testing

entry.title: Window Size Presets 1.0.0
entry.content:
Window Size Presets

Resize any window to a preset size, natively, in the spirit of Sizer.

Ways to open the preset menu

  • Title bar button - right-click and/or hover the minimise (or maximise) button. Configurable in the settings; right-click is the default.
  • Hotkey - opens the menu for the foreground window at the mouse cursor.

Presets

Add as many as you like in the settings. Each preset has:

  • Name (optional) - label shown in the menu.
  • Width / Height - in pixels or as a percentage of the monitor's work area. 0 keeps the current value. At least one of them must be non-zero, and the first preset with both set to 0 ends the list.
  • Position - keep, centre, or snap to a corner of the work area.

A tick is shown next to the preset matching the window's current size and position.

Notes

  • This is a tool mod: it runs in its own dedicated windhawk.exe process and doesn't inject into any other process.
  • Windows running as administrator can't be resized unless Windhawk's tool process is also elevated (UIPI).
  • On Windows 11, hovering the maximise button also opens the Snap Layouts flyout, so the minimise button is the better choice for hover.
  • The Winstant mod also reacts to hovering the minimise button. If you use both, give them different buttons or triggers (for example, right-click for this mod).
  • Changing any setting is applied immediately, without restarting the mod.

entry.title: Per-monitor taskbar icon alignment 1.0.0
entry.content:
Per-monitor taskbar icon alignment

Choose how the taskbar looks on each monitor separately: its icons Left, Center, Right or Windows' default, and the Start button at the left edge, the right edge, or with the icons. Windows only offers one alignment for every taskbar, and only Left or Center.

| Icons | Start button | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Left | with the icons | | | Center | with the icons | | | Right | with the icons | | | Center | left edge | | | Left | right edge | |

Settings

  • Primary monitor / Other monitors set the icon alignment and the Start button placement for every monitor of that kind. Windows default keeps whatever Windows is set to. Out of the box the primary monitor keeps Windows' own alignment and the other monitors are Left.
  • Per-monitor overrides handle individual displays: add one row per monitor and pick it from the Monitor dropdown, 1st to 6th from the left or Rightmost. Positions follow the arrangement in Windows display settings, so they keep working when displays are renumbered or reconnected. Choose Custom to type a display device name (DISPLAY1), a monitor name (DELL U2719D) or part of a device path (DISPLAY#DELA0C1) instead. The first matching row wins.
  • Start button: Follow the icons leaves it in the icon group, as Windows does. Left edge and Right edge (next to the tray) place it independently, and the icons close the gap. Choosing the edge the icons already gather at changes nothing.

Right is this mod's own option: Windows' alignment setting has no Right, so a Right taskbar is told Left and its icons are aligned right in the taskbar's layout, stopping at the system tray. The tray itself never moves.

Installation

Install the mod. It takes over the running taskbars straight away, and also after an update or when you disable and enable it, and changing settings applies immediately. If a taskbar doesn't change, for instance after a Windows update has changed the taskbar's internals, restart Windows Explorer once (Task Manager > Windows Explorer > Restart). Enable Show my taskbar on all displays in Windows settings to get a taskbar on every monitor.

Disabling the mod puts every taskbar back to Windows' own layout.

Compatibility

Windows 11, 64-bit, native taskbar only. Tested on Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300) with Windhawk 1.7.3, on three displays with different resolutions and scales.

The mod relies on Windows' private taskbar internals. A Windows update can change them: if the core hooks can't be found the mod refuses to start, and the XAML-based features (Right icons, Start button placement) simply stay off. Windows 10 is not supported. Start menu and search flyouts keep using Windows' own placement. No registry values are changed. See below for tools that change the taskbar themselves.

Known limit: the Widgets button isn't taken into account, so with Widgets shown the Start button's Left edge may overlap it, and so may Right icons or the Right edge on a taskbar where Windows moves it.

Other taskbar tools can interfere

Apps and mods that add their own taskbar features, such as Start11, StartAllBack, ExplorerPatcher or other Windhawk taskbar mods, can take over how the taskbar buttons are drawn and laid out. Center, Right and the Start button placement can then look wrong or not apply, whatever this mod does.

A known case is Start11's "Let Start11 enhance the taskbar". It draws the taskbar buttons itself, in its own window laid over the taskbar, so the buttons this mod positions are not the ones you see. With Right, for example, only some of the buttons may show up, cut off on the left:

If you see this, open Start11, go to Taskbar and turn Let Start11 enhance the taskbar off (or use the option below it, Disable all taskbar features for compatibility with other taskbar mods), then restart Explorer. The page should look like this:

For any other tool, switch its taskbar features off for a moment to check whether they are the cause.

Source, build instructions and tests: https://github.com/VitalyTz/windhawk-taskbar-per-monitor-alignment

entry.title: Win+E Reuse File Explorer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Win+E Reuse File Explorer

Press Win+E to bring the most recently active File Explorer window forward. Minimized windows are restored. If Explorer is already focused, it stays focused.

If no Explorer window exists on the current virtual desktop, Windows handles Win+E normally and opens a new window. Extra modifiers (Ctrl, Shift, or Alt) are left unchanged. There are no settings.

entry.title: Notification Center Follows Taskbar 1.0.0
entry.content:
Notification Center Follows Taskbar

Keeps the Windows 11 Notification Center (Win+N, including its calendar) correctly positioned with top, bottom, left, and right taskbars. Detects the taskbar on the flyout's monitor automatically. Adds the missing correction for top taskbars, with an 8 logical pixel vertical gap; retains the horizontal position chosen by Windows or other mods. Auto-hidden taskbars use the monitor's working area.

Install alongside your taskbar positioning mod. Close and reopen Notification Center after enabling, disabling, or moving the taskbar.

Enable Swap notifications and calendar to put the calendar above the notifications. The panels exchange their visual positions while Windows keeps control of their native layout sizes and scrolling. The combined outer bounds stay fixed: the swap doesn't move the host window or change row definitions. No fixed notification height is used. Expanding/collapsing the calendar and changing display size use Windows' normal layout calculations.

Remove any Notification Center Styler rules that swap these panels or force their heights, row definitions, or row positions before enabling this option. Cosmetic styling can remain. Switching the option off restores the original transforms, including bindings. The positioning fix works without the swap.

Other positioning mods

The top-taskbar fix changes only Y by default, so horizontal alignment from Shell Flyout Positions is preserved. This mod and Shell Flyout Positions both observe the flyout being uncloaked; they should not both force its X coordinate.

Repair right-edge position after Explorer restarts is optional. It forces right alignment for top taskbars and overrides a left/center alignment selected in another mod. Leave it off when using Shell Flyout Positions. It is retained because we observed a surviving shell host occasionally reopening on the left after Explorer/taskbar recreation; forcing right alignment corrected that case.

ShellExperienceHost loads this mod only while panel swapping is enabled. Window creation only schedules initialization; XAML is accessed later on its UI thread.

Fix Task Manager Icon Sizes

entry.title: Radial Window Switcher 1.0.0
entry.content:
Radial Window Switcher

Replaces the standard Alt+Tab with a radial switcher: the icons of open windows are arranged in a ring in the center of the screen, the name of the selected app is shown in the middle, and a live preview of the selected window appears next to its sector.

Usage

  • Hold Alt and press Tab to open the ring.
  • While holding Alt, press Tab for the next window, Shift+Tab for the previous one. Arrow keys also work.
  • Release Alt to switch to the selected window.
  • Press Esc to close the ring without switching.
  • A quick Alt+Tab switches to the previous window, just like the standard one.

Features

  • Smooth animations: the ring spins in, sectors pop out one by one, the selection glows and a pointer glides to the selected app.
  • Live window previews (DWM thumbnails), like the standard Alt+Tab.
  • The selected sector uses the Windows accent color.
  • Per-monitor DPI aware; the ring opens on the monitor with the cursor.
  • Can use Alt+` or Alt+Q instead of Alt+Tab, keeping the standard switcher.

Notes

  • The switcher runs in its own Windhawk process. Only a small part runs in Explorer: it catches Explorer's Alt+Tab hotkey and hands it to the switcher, so the standard switcher doesn't open as well.
  • Minimized windows have no preview: Windows doesn't render them.
  • Alt+` and Alt+Q can't be caught while an elevated (administrator) window is in the foreground. Alt+Tab works there too, through Explorer.

entry.title: Secondary windows on the active monitor 2.1
entry.content:
Secondary windows on the active monitor

Useful if you have several monitors. Many apps remember which monitor a secondary window (media viewer, player, dialog) was opened on and open it there again, even if you now work with the app on another monitor. For example, Telegram Desktop opens photos and videos on the monitor where the viewer was last time, not where the chat is.

The mod intercepts the showing of secondary windows of the apps from the Applications list and, if a window is about to appear on a different monitor than the app's active window, moves it to the active window's monitor before it is shown. By default the list contains a placeholder (test.exe), replace it with your app, for example Telegram Desktop (Telegram.exe); add any other app by its executable name in the mod settings.

For apps that are not built with Qt, the mod decides which windows are regular ones by a heuristic (it skips menus, tooltips, tool windows and the like), so it may move something it shouldn't, such as a drop-down list or a splash screen. Telegram is the only app the mod was tested with; if another app misbehaves, use the Window title filter of that app.

Which windows are moved: all secondary windows of the app that get their own window - for Telegram also picture-in-picture video, call windows and chats opened in a separate window. Menus, tooltips, notifications and tool windows are not moved. If you keep some windows on another monitor on purpose, set a Window title filter for the app to limit the mod to windows with a given title.

How a window is placed:

  • it keeps its relative position on the screen (a window in the top right corner of one monitor appears in the top right corner of the other);
  • a window larger than the target monitor is shrunk to fit;
  • a fullscreen window stays fullscreen;
  • a maximized window stays maximized, and when restored it stays on the new monitor;
  • monitors with different scaling are taken into account.

Keeping the position and accounting for scaling can each be turned off in the settings.

The mod is loaded into every process and unloads itself at once from those that are not in the Applications list. An app added to the list starts to work after it is restarted; removing an app from the list applies immediately.

System files and app data are not modified.

entry.title: Disable Task Manager Navigation Border 0.1
entry.content:
Disable Task Manager Navigation Border

Disables the ugly focus borders in Windows 11 Task Manager.

It works by replacing the following functions with empty implementations:

  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForColumnHeader
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRow
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRowWithColumnTraversal
  • SetBorderUponNavigatingIntoElement

Functions are located using symbols for the running Taskmgr.exe version, not fixed addresses. First use may require internet access to download symbols. Initialization fails if any required symbol is unavailable.

This MOD targets x64 Task Manager versions providing these methods. No system files or signatures are modified.

禁用 Windows 11 任务管理器上丑陋的焦点边框。

实现原理是将以下方法替换为空实现：

  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForColumnHeader
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRow
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRowWithColumnTraversal
  • SetBorderUponNavigatingIntoElement

这些函数是通过当前运行的 Taskmgr.exe 版本的符号信息进行定位，而非固定内存地址。首次使用可能需要联网下载符号文件。若缺少任何所需符号，初始化将失败。

此 MOD 适用于包含上述方法的 x64 版本任务管理器。不会修改任何系统文件或签名。

entry.title: Flashlight Desktop Icons 1.0.0
entry.content:
Flashlight Desktop Icons

Makes desktop icons semi-transparent (or completely invisible) when idle. When the mouse cursor moves over the desktop, only the icons within the configured pixel radius smoothly reveal themselves, and they fade back to their idle opacity once the mouse stops moving.

  • No overlay windows: each icon's alpha is applied at draw time with GDI custom draw, so nothing blocks clicks and no wallpaper layers are duplicated. Compatible with Wallpaper Engine and other live wallpapers.
  • No background threads and no polling: repainting is driven by mouse events and a fade timer running on the desktop's own thread, so the mod does no work at all while the mouse is away from the desktop.
  • Labels fade together with their icons. Enable the "Hide Icon Labels" setting to remove the text under desktop icons entirely.
  • Dragging a file over the desktop reveals the icons around the drag cursor, so you can see what you are dropping onto.
  • Double-clicking empty desktop space hides all icons; double-clicking again returns to flashlight mode (rather than making all icons fully visible).

How this differs from similar mods

  • Transparent Desktop Icons with Spotlight reveals icons around the cursor using a DirectComposition overlay mask. This mod instead computes each icon's alpha from its distance to the cursor and applies it per icon at draw time (GDI custom draw), with no overlay or wallpaper layers.
  • Desktop Icons Transparency applies one fixed opacity to all desktop icons. This mod's opacity is per-icon and follows the cursor.
  • Desktop Icon Section Auto-Hide & Fluent Hover Reveal and ZenDesktop hide and reveal icons in bulk (per section or on toggle). This mod's default experience is a continuous visibility gradient around the cursor.

Known limitations

  • Faded labels are drawn in the mod's own style (white text with a glow) rather than Explorer's shadow style, so a label changes slightly when its icon reaches full opacity and Explorer takes over drawing it.

Credits

  • desktop-icons-transparency by zed712969-crypto: desktop window discovery and subclassing patterns.
  • Smooth Desktop Icons Auto-Hide by HeyOkay: the drag-and-drop reveal approach (hooking the desktop's IDropTarget vtable methods).

entry.title: Alt.Binz Dark Mode 1.0.0
entry.content:
Alt.Binz Dark Mode

Alt.Binz draws its whole user interface from a light blue skin. This mod re-colors everything that is drawn with GDI: brushes, pens, text colors, system colors and the opaque skin bitmaps. Common dialogs and shell menus keep Windows' own dark mode.

Compatibility

Tested with Alt.Binz 0.48.4 (32-bit) at 100% display scaling on Windows 11. Some elements (the column header bars, the progress bar fills and the status bar button) are recognized by their size and color, so another version may look different.

Surface color

The blue skin surface (toolbar, tabs, status bar, dialogs, Setup) can get another color: enter a hex code (for example 2F5A96). Very bright colors are darkened so that the light text stays readable.

Surface gradient

Instead of one color the surface can run between two colors. Enter both as hex codes, the angle in degrees (0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom) and the balance: 50 is the middle, a higher value gives the end color more room, a lower value the start color. The gradient wins over the single surface color.

Progress bars

The fill of the progress bars can get one color or, with a second color, a gradient, either from top to bottom or from left to right. Leave both empty for the default blue.

Appearance

These values are applied when Alt.Binz is restarted:

  • Background lightness: how dark the lists and dark areas are (percent).
  • Text lightness: how bright text and lines are (percent). Ignored when a text color is set.
  • Text color: an optional color for text and lines.
  • List background color: an optional color for the large list areas.
  • Saturation: how colorful the blue skin is (percent).

The column header color (the header bars of the lists) and everything else is applied live. If you disable the mod, restart Alt.Binz to get the original look back completely.

entry.title: PaintShop Pro Dark Image Windows 1.0.0
entry.content:
PaintShop Pro Dark Image Windows

Corel PaintShop Pro has a dark theme, but the image windows inside the workspace keep a light blue-gray frame that looks like Windows XP or 7. They are classic MDI child windows, and Windows draws their frames itself, with no dark variant.

This mod paints those frames in dark colors instead:

  • title bar, border, icon and title text
  • minimize, maximize and close buttons with hover and pressed states
  • minimized image windows

Maximized image windows are left to Windows. Everything is drawn by the mod, so no theme files or system settings are touched, and the mod only affects PaintShop Pro.

Optional flash fix

When you switch between images, PaintShop Pro rebuilds the drop-down lists in the tool options bar. For a few frames their selection fields flash white, because the Windows combo box falls back to its default brush. The flash fix paints that field in dark gray instead.

Settings

All colors are entered as hex codes, for example 282828 or #282828. A value that cannot be read falls back to its default. Changes apply right away.

Notes

  • Tested with PaintShop Pro 2022 on Windows 11. Other versions may work, but have not been tested.
  • If something looks wrong, disable the mod: the original frames come back immediately.

entry.title: App Volume Booster 1.0
entry.content:
App Volume Booster

Changes the loudness of the audio an app sends to Windows, so it can go past the 100% limit of the volume mixer.

This mod doesn't target any process by default.

Which apps: open this mod's Advanced tab -> Custom process inclusion list and list the exe names you want affected (one per line). Only those processes get the mod. Restart an app after adding it to the list.

Note for games: Games are excluded by default in Windhawk. To work with games, they need to be specifically added to the inclusion list from Windhawk's Advanced settings: Settings > Advanced settings > More advanced settings > Process Inclusion List.

How loud: every included app uses the default settings. To give one app its own settings, click + under Per-app overrides, type its exe name and choose its volume and mode. An override only applies to apps that are also in the inclusion list. Overrides with an empty process name are ignored.

Modes

  • Gain (default): multiplies the audio by the volume %. 100 = unchanged, 200 = twice as loud. Anything pushed past full scale is clipped.
  • Compressor: turns down the loud parts, then applies the volume % as makeup gain, so quiet material gets louder with less distortion on loud peaks. Tune it with threshold, ratio, attack and release (these settings are shared by all apps).

Changes apply live. Lower your system volume before starting, boosted audio can be very loud. Exclusive-mode streams, spatial audio streams (e.g. Windows Sonic / Dolby Atmos, which bypass IAudioRenderClient), and apps that bypass WASAPI entirely may not be affected.

Troubleshooting: start the app after enabling the mod (streams created earlier are not seen), then check Windhawk's log for this mod. It reports each stream's format and whether audio is being processed.

entry.title: GPU-accelerated explorer.exe list and grid views 0.9.240
entry.content:
GPU-accelerated explorer.exe list and grid views

A Windhawk mod for Windows 11 Explorer with GPU rendering for smooth animations and modern look.

  • Replicates explorer views using hardware accelerated graphics: Details list and icons grid, including thumbnails, sorting and grouping.
  • Animated interactions: grouping, sorting, selecting/cutting/copying files, and many more.
  • Smooth scrolling, touchpad gestures and inertia scrolling.
  • RTL language support.
  • Optional button to switch back to native Explorer view; Ctrl+Alt+F9 also works when the button is hidden.
  • Prioritizes responsiveness and animations over efficiency.
  • Less likely to break in future Windows updates since it does not modify the default views of explorer but recreates them

Features

  • Adjustable Item Height — Smooth zooming with Ctrl+ mouse wheel or pinch gestures.
  • Custom Fonts — Personalize the appearance with your preferred fonts.
  • Text Antialiasing — Use Windows monitor tuning, smooth grayscale, or no antialiasing while preserving transparent backgrounds.
  • Animated Selection & Hover States — Smooth visual transitions, including a dedicated selection style for file names only.
  • Dynamic Zebra Striping — Animated alternating row colors for improved readability.
  • Smooth Scrolling — Fluid scrolling for a more responsive browsing experience.
  • Seamless View Switching — Overlays the default Explorer views, letting you switch between the modded and native views directly from the Explorer window.
  • Faster Loading — Improves load times through caching and by skipping file pre-sorting.
  • Adaptive Image Quality — Matches icon and thumbnail resolution to visible size and available memory.

Report bugs

Report bugs in the mod's main repository Here. Enable Enable logging when reproducing a bug and include Windhawk's log in the report. Logs include file names and paths; disable the option afterward.
